original_record.question:
Lisas aviation club designs a flag with a flying "dove" on a $4 \times 6$-grid. The area of the "dove" is $192 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$. The perimeter of the "dove" is made up of straight lines and circular arcs. What measurements does the flag have?
<image1>
original_record.subject: combinatorial geometry

inventory.dove: four quarter-circle arcs radius2, joined to straight lower/left wing edges through(1,1)

audit.layout_only: Frozen uniform scale and placement; source orientation retained.

answer_verification.reason: Two added quarter disks cancel two removed quarter disks; dove area is12 grid units². 192/12=16 per cell, cell side4, flag24x16.

self_review.facts: Four curved arcs and two straight bird edges preserved on6x4 grid; no lost cell lines or clipping.
